definitions.explanation: The practice of attaching the honorific suffix さん to a person's name when addressing or referring to them. Indicates a basic level of politeness and respect.

examples.japanese: {職場|しょくば}ではさん{付|づ}けが{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: In the workplace, using -san is the norm.

examples.japanese: うちの{会社|かいしゃ}はさん{付|づ}けで{呼|よ}び{合|あ}う。
examples.english: At our company, we address each other with -san.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}にも{部下|ぶか}にもさん{付|づ}けで{呼|よ}ぶようにしている{会社|かいしゃ}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More companies are adopting the practice of addressing both superiors and subordinates with -san.

notes:
The word {付|づ}け means 'attaching' or 'affixing,' so さん{付|づ}け literally means 'attaching さん.' This pattern is productive: ちゃん{付|づ}け (using -chan), くん{付|づ}け (using -kun), {様|さま}{付|づ}け (using -sama) all follow the same structure. In many Japanese workplaces, there has been a trend toward さん{付|づ}け as a way to create a more egalitarian atmosphere, replacing {役職|やくしょく}{呼|よ}び (addressing by job title).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- さん{付|づ}けで{呼|よ}ぶ: to address with -san
- さん{付|づ}けが{基本|きほん}: -san is the standard
- さん{付|づ}けルール: -san rule (company policy)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- ちゃん{付|づ}け: using -chan — more familiar, for children or close relationships
- くん{付|づ}け: using -kun — used toward male peers or subordinates
- {呼|よ}び{捨|す}て: calling someone by name without an honorific — considered rude unless the relationship is very close
